pull.title: wallet: return broadcast errors from CommitTransaction
pull.body:
Part of https://github.com/bitcoin-core/gui-qml/issues/1008.

The QML GUI shows "Transaction sent" even when the node rejected the transaction, because `CWallet::CommitTransaction()` only logs the rejection and returns `void`. 
This PR bubbles up the submission result through `interfaces::Wallet::commitTransaction()` so the GUI can report it.

#### Key changes
- Introduce `TransactionBroadcastError`, holding a `TransactionError` code and an untranslated message.
- Commit/Broadcast functions returns `Expected<void, TransactionBroadcastError>`. 
  - Remove `TransactionError::OK`, a success value in an error enum.
- Add a `SUBMISSION_SKIPPED` code for when the wallet doesn't submit the transaction (broadcasting disabled, abandoned, coinbase, confirmed or conflicted). `SubmitTxMemoryPoolAndRelay()` previously returned `false` in these cases.

#### Note
- Existing callers (wallet RPCs, Qt widgets, fee bumper) ignore the new result, so their behavior and RPC responses don't change.
- `commitBumpTransaction()` similarly reports success for a rejected replacement. This will be addressed in a follow-up PR.
- gui-qml will need to update its `interfaces::Wallet` mock for the new `commitTransaction()` signature.

events.message:
refactor: use Expected for transaction broadcast results

Introduce TransactionBroadcastError, which holds a TransactionError and
a message. BroadcastTransaction returns
Expected<void, TransactionBroadcastError>, so the error code and its message
travel together. Remove TransactionError::OK.

Errors that had an empty message now carry the generic
TransactionErrorString text.

wallet: report skipped transaction submissions

Return Expected<void, TransactionBroadcastError> from
SubmitTxMemoryPoolAndRelay. Wallet-side prechecks (broadcasting
disabled, coinbase, abandoned, confirmed or conflicted) return the new
SUBMISSION_SKIPPED code with a reason; node errors pass through.

wallet: propagate submission errors through commit APIs

Return the submission result from CWallet::CommitTransaction and
interfaces::Wallet::commitTransaction, so callers can tell whether a
saved transaction was accepted.

test: cover CommitTransaction results

Check the CommitTransaction result for accepted, already confirmed,
max-fee and mempool-minimum rejections, and that a rejected transaction
stays saved in the wallet.

Also check the result through interfaces::Wallet::commitTransaction,
which the GUI uses, for skipped and accepted commits.

Concept ACK 4e3d1675597173075a7efd9b3905c928b2be8de5

With -walletbroadcast=0, commitTransaction now returns an error (SUBMISSION_SKIPPED), even though the user chose not to broadcast. Will the QML GUI treat that as "saved, not broadcast" rather than as a failure?

> Concept ACK [4e3d167](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/4e3d1675597173075a7efd9b3905c928b2be8de5)
> 
> With -walletbroadcast=0, commitTransaction now returns an error (SUBMISSION_SKIPPED), even though the user chose not to broadcast. Will the QML GUI treat that as "saved, not broadcast" rather than as a failure?

Yes, that's the intent. `SUBMISSION_SKIPPED` is a separate code precisely so a caller can differentiate between "the wallet didn't submit it" and "the node rejected it" and act accordingly.

Can you explain why this would be needed? If the wallet creates a consensus-invalid (permanently invalid) transaction, that seems like a severe bug that should be fixed instead. If the wallet creates a tx which permanently fails the mempool policy, that seems like an equally severe bug that should be fixed instead. If the wallet creates a tx that undershoots the fee, that seems irrelevant and can equally happen when the tx was accepted to the mempool, but then dropped? If the mempool min fee is 0.677 sat/vB, but the user explicitly asked for a tx at `0.1`, it seems like a case that the GUI should not allow or display a warning while creating the tx. Some feedback directly  after the tx was created seems misplaced? If this was needed, the feedback could be done async?

> If the wallet creates a consensus-invalid (permanently invalid) transaction, that seems like a severe bug that should be fixed instead. If the wallet creates a tx which permanently fails the mempool policy, that seems like an equally severe bug that should be fixed instead.

The GUI can import a PSBT that spends the wallet's coins, sign it with the wallet and commit it. Its inputs and fee were chosen elsewhere and none of `createTransaction()`'s checks ran, so a rejection (fee above `-maxtxfee`, a non-standard output, a mempool conflict) isn't a wallet bug and can't be caught at creation. An early rejection with the reason at `commitTransaction()` time seems useful.

> If the wallet creates a tx that undershoots the fee, that seems irrelevant and can equally happen when the tx was accepted to the mempool, but then dropped? If the mempool min fee is 0.677 sat/vB, but the user explicitly asked for a tx at 0.1, it seems like a case that the GUI should not allow or display a warning while creating the tx. 

Partially agree. The GUI should catch this before the user confirms. Currently, it looks like `GetMinimumFeeRate()` only checks `-mintxfee`/`-minrelaytxfee` when the user has set the fee rate manually. Maybe GUI should also check for mempool minimum.

> Some feedback directly after the tx was created seems misplaced?  If this was needed, the feedback could be done async?

A synchronous error when submission fails right away seems more useful than returning `void`, which is what we do today. 
Async feedback sounds like a good idea. Something the GUI can subscribe to and be notified about (a later eviction). I see it as complementing the sync error rather than replacing it.
